title: Sarawak Haze Hits Hazardous Levels as Regional Crisis Becomes Worst Since 2015
detail: Six air-quality monitoring areas in Malaysia's Sarawak state recorded hazardous API readings on the morning of Sept. 1 — Serian 408, Kuching 402-407, Samarahan 371-372, Sri Aman 361-364, Sarikei 333-337, and Sibu 309-315 — as cross-border smoke from Indonesian Borneo peatland fires intensified. Sarawak health data showed asthma cases surging to 1,811 for the week of Aug. 23-29, up from 219 the prior week, with conjunctivitis cases rising to 720 from 146. Deputy Premier Douglas Uggah Embas warned that any area crossing API 500 would trigger emergency closure of non-essential services. Al Jazeera described the episode, which has directly exposed roughly 5.5 million people across Borneo and Sumatra, as the region's worst transboundary haze crisis since 2015, when Indonesian fires sickened more than 500,000 people.

media.caption: Haze from Indonesian forest fires shrouds the region as air quality hits hazardous levels in Sarawak

title: El Niño Deals 'Devastating Blow' to Peru's Anchovy Industry as 122,000 Jobs Seen Lost
detail: Peru's National Fisheries Society (SNP) said El Niño-driven warming — sea-surface temperatures up to 6°C above normal in some areas — has crushed the country's anchovy catch, with May 2026 landings of just 32,800 metric tons versus 1.3 million tons in May 2025. Fishing's contribution to Peru's GDP fell to an estimated 1.1% in 2026 from 2.1% in 2025. SNP president Jessica Luna said the industry, which normally generates 250,000 jobs, is projected to lose 122,000 of them by next year, calling it 'a devastating blow to the sector.' Displaced fishermen in Chimbote and Callao described shifting into public transport, construction, and mining work as anchovy stocks stay dispersed in cooler, deeper water.

media.caption: El Niño-warmed seas have crushed Peru's anchovy catch, threatening 122,000 jobs
